mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, which in turn results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real GDP indicates strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where GDP growth is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in industrial production by more than 1% over the last two months indicates a supply-side contraction, which leads to reduced economic output and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both housing starts and retail sales signals a strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where both proxies show positive growth.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate signals a strengthening labor market, which leads to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where both proxies indicate a strengthening labor market.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index over the last three months signals inflationary pressures, which leads to increased costs for businesses and reduced real earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where CPI growth is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in retail sales combined with a decrease in housing starts signals a weakening consumer demand, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and investor sentiment, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where both proxies show negative growth.
